findings.why_it_matters: Nobody is accountable for this app: no one will rotate its credentials, review its permissions or retire it, and a forgotten app keeps working for whoever holds its credentials.
findings.how_to_verify_manually: Entra admin center > App registrations > All applications > app > Owners; GET /v1.0/applications/1703235f-b665-5109-b8a2-1dd25b227262/owners

findings.why_it_matters: Permissions nobody uses are pure exposure: the identity can still be signed in as, but nothing would break if it were disabled.
findings.how_to_verify_manually: Entra admin center > Monitoring > Usage & insights > Service principal sign-in activity; GET /beta/reports/servicePrincipalSignInActivities?$filter=appId eq '04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46'

findings.why_it_matters: A secret that stays valid for years gives anyone who copies it years of access; short lifetimes force rotation and limit the damage of a leak.

findings.why_it_matters: Expired credentials left in place show nobody is managing this identity's lifecycle and hide which credential is really in use.

findings.why_it_matters: A client secret is a shared password that can be pasted anywhere; a certificate key can be kept non-exportable, and federation removes the stored credential altogether.

findings.why_it_matters: A federated credential lets an outside workload sign in as this app with no secret; the subject is the only thing that decides which workload, so a loose subject hands the app's permissions to more code than intended.
findings.how_to_verify_manually: Entra admin center > App registrations > app > Certificates & secrets > Federated credentials; GET /beta/applications/2c339056-3f55-5d2a-9e74-5def96e73917/federatedIdentityCredentials

findings.why_it_matters: If the same identity serves test and production, a compromise of the weaker test pipeline or host reaches production data.

findings.why_it_matters: Without a workload identity policy a stolen credential works from any network; a location or risk policy is the control that limits where the app can sign in from.
findings.how_to_verify_manually: Entra admin center > Conditional Access > Policies (Assignments > Workload identities); GET /v1.0/identity/conditionalAccess/policies

findings.why_it_matters: Whoever can add a credential to a privileged service principal can sign in as it and use all of its permissions, so these people and apps are as privileged as the identity itself.
findings.how_to_verify_manually: For each step: Entra admin center > App registrations > app > Owners; Roles & admins > role > Assignments; Groups > group > Members/Owners. Graph: GET /v1.0/applications/{id}/owners, GET /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments

findings.why_it_matters: When a person signs in as a service account, its actions can no longer be told apart from the automation's, and the account's standing access becomes that person's.
findings.how_to_verify_manually: Entra admin center > Monitoring > Sign-in logs (filter: user, Interactive); GET /v1.0/auditLogs/signIns?$filter=userId eq '22dc1af0-e8f2-5559-946d-80e49575ac1c'
